Assigned Readings & Foundational Scholarship

Please study the following foundational works on digital scholarly edition design, peer review, and long-term sustainability:

  • Sahle, Patrick. "What is a Digital Scholarly Edition?" In Digital Scholarly Editing: Theories and Practices, ed. M. J. Driscoll and E. Pierazzo, Open Book Publishers, 2016, pp. 19–39.
  • Pierazzo, Elena. Digital Textual Scholarship: Theories, Methods and Common Practices. Ashgate/Routledge, 2015. Chapters 4 (Modelling) and 5 (Publishing).
  • El Khatib, Randa. "Drawing Digital Scholarship into the Academic Conversation: The Exigency of Early Modern Digital Review" (Ch. 3). In NTMRS 11, Iter Press, 2023, pp. 55–73 (Open Access).
  • Meneses, Luis. "Extending the Contribution of Online Digital Projects about the Middle Ages and Renaissance: A Case Study of DEx" (Ch. 8). In NTMRS 11, Iter Press, 2023, pp. 171–188 (Open Access).
  • Hendriksen, Marieke M. A. "Data That Last: Reflections on Sustainability in Digital Humanities Projects" (Ch. 11). In NTMRS 11, Iter Press, 2023, pp. 245–258 (Open Access).
